Head: Logic
Path: 一. Logic
Gloss: The structure of reality and, in the same concepts, of thought: the basic determinations all thinking relies on, each leading to the next. Then the study of these concepts in their own right and in that order.
Nouns: logic, science of logic; speculative logic, dialectical logic, objective logic, subjective logic; dialectic, dialectics; science of thought, science of pure reason; pure thought; thinking, ratiocination &c (inference) H0165. metaphysics, first philosophy, ontology, theory of categories; table of categories. thought thinking itself; reason; realm of shadows; the system of pure reason; categories, predicaments†, forms of thought. the system of categories.
Verbs: think, reason, ratiocinate, cogitate, excogitate†; think through, think out, follow out, carry through; reason a priori; categorize; deduce, derive, develop, unfold; logicize, syllogize &c H0165. reflect. draw an inference.
Adjective: logical, dialectical, speculative, categorial, ontological, metaphysical; pure, formal, abstract; presuppositionless; rational, noetic, intelligible; systematic, immanent, self-developing. reflective. intellectual, mental.
Adverbs: logically, dialectically &c adj.; in thought, in pure thought, in the element of thought.

Head: Doctrine of Being
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being
Gloss: The study of the simplest concepts, those that describe a thing directly as it is, without reference to anything behind it. Each such concept, when thought through, gives way to another.
Nouns: doctrine of being; logic of being, ontology; immediacy, directness, givenness, the given, datum, data; surface, face value; transition, passing over; change into another &c (becoming) H0007. the in-itself; being-in-itself; the concept in itself, latency, implicitness, potentiality; first sphere, outset, threshold. categories of being, immediate categories; what simply is, what there is; brute fact, plain fact, bare fact. beginning, commencement, inception. the sphere of immediacy, quality quantity and measure.
Verbs: be, exist, obtain, be given, lie to hand; pass over, pass into, go over into, turn into, give way to, change into; follow upon; lie on the surface. have being, subsist. become.
Adjective: immediate, unmediated, direct, given, simple, bare, plain, raw; ontic, ontological, existential; implicit, latent, potential, inchoate, rudimentary, undeveloped; transitional, transitive, passing, transient; first, initial, primary, elementary. mere, sheer.
Adverbs: immediately, directly, simply, barely, at first sight, at face value, on the face of it; in itself; in the first instance.

Head: Determinateness (Quality)
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality)

Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › α. Being › a. Pure Being

Head: Something and Other
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › b. Finitude › i. Something and Other
Gloss: The relation of a thing to what it is not. Each side is "something" and each is the "other" of the other, so which is which depends on point of view.
Nouns: something and other; the other, otherness, alterity; difference &c H0089; the alien, the foreign, the stranger, the outsider; the not-self, non-ego; counterpart, opposite number, complement, foil; relativity, perspective, point of view, standpoint; being-for-other; being-in-itself; self and other, us and them, this and that, ego and alter. the something.
Verbs: be other, differ, be distinct, stand apart; other, alienate, estrange, defamiliarize; relate to, stand in relation to; contrast, compare, set against. relate to another.
Adjective: other, another, else, different, distinct, separate; alien, foreign, strange, outlandish, extraneous, external; relative, relational, reciprocal, mutual, correlative, perspectival. not the same, unequal &c H0045. unrelated, independent. ulterior. interrelated, complementary.
Adverbs: otherwise, else, differently; on the other hand, conversely; relatively, from another point of view.
Foreign: German: das Andere, Anderssein, Sein-für-Anderes, Ansichsein, Etwas und Anderes; Latin: alteritas, alter ego, per contra, vice versa; Greek: heterotēs, to heteron; Arabic: ghayr [other]; Sanskrit: anātman; Chinese: ta [other].
Phrases: alter ego [Lat.]; l'enfer, c'est les autres [Fr.] [Sartre]; je est un autre [Fr.] [Rimbaud]; one man's meat is another man's poison.

Head: Determination, Constitution, and Limit
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › b. Finitude › ii. Determination, Constitution, and Limit
Gloss: Three ways a thing is defined: its determination, what it is essentially; its constitution, what it happens to be through outside circumstance; and its limit, the boundary where it stops and something else begins.
Nouns: determination, vocation, destiny, calling, purpose, end, in-itself, inner nature; constitution, make-up, condition, state, circumstance, situation, disposition, external character, accidental nature; limit, boundary, border, bound, bourn†, frontier, edge, margin, brink, verge, rim, periphery, confines, pale, march, marches; terminus, term, horizon, ceiling, threshold, line, demarcation, delimitation, circumscription. habitude, diathesis†, fabric &c H0258, stamp, set, fit, mold, mould. category, estate, lot, mood, temper, aspect &c H0387, dilemma, pass, predicament. phase, position, posture, attitude, place, point, terms, regime, footing, standing, status. bounds, enclave, curbstone†, but, reservation, termination, stint, precinct, backwoods.
Verbs: determine, destine, ordain, appoint, fix; constitute, condition, dispose, frame, shape; limit, bound, delimit, demarcate, circumscribe, confine, restrict, hem in, fence in, wall in, draw the line, mark off, mark out. inclose, surround &c H0218, compass about, hedge in, rail in, fence round, hedge round.
Adjective: determined, destined, fated, intended; constituted, conditioned, circumstanced, situated; limited, bounded, bordered, circumscribed, confined, restricted, terminal, marginal, peripheral, liminal, borderline, frontier. definite, conterminate†, conterminable†, bordering. qualifying, qualified, hedged, conditional, exceptional &c H0063.
Adverbs: within limits, within bounds, within the pale; at the limit, on the edge, on the verge, on the brink; up to a point, so far and no further. by nature, by circumstance.
Foreign: German: Beschaffenheit, Grenze, Bestimmung; Latin: finis, terminus; Greek: telos, peras [limit]; Arabic: ḥadd; Sanskrit: sīmā [boundary]; Chinese: jie [boundary].
Phrases: ne plus ultra [Lat.]; hitherto shalt thou come, but no further [Bible]; est modus in rebus, sunt certi denique fines [Lat.] [Horace]; good fences make good neighbours [Frost].

Head: Finitude as Such
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › b. Finitude › iii. Finitude as Such
Gloss: Limitedness taken seriously: a thing whose limit is part of its very nature, so that it is bound to pass away; mortality, transience.
Nouns: finitude as such; mortality, the mortal condition, being-toward-death; perishability, transience, transitoriness, ephemerality, evanescence, fragility, frailty, vulnerability, precariousness, caducity; destined end, appointed end, doom, fate, lot; impermanence; vanity; the dust, dust and ashes; death's-head, skull, hourglass, guttering candle. finite things &c H0016. finiteness, limitedness, perishableness.
Verbs: perish, pass away, die, expire, decay, fade, wither, crumble, moulder; be numbered, have one's days numbered; be bound to die. cease to exist &c H0004, die out, disappear &c H0009. flit, vanish. end, run out.
Adjective: mortal, perishable, perishing, ephemeral, transient, fleeting, fugitive, evanescent, short-lived, momentary, frail, fragile, brittle, precarious, vulnerable; doomed, fated, foredoomed, condemned; sublunary, earthly, terrestrial, creaturely. transitory, passing. temporal, temporary, impermanent. finite.
Adverbs: in the end, at last, sooner or later; till death; for a season. finitely.
Foreign: German: Sein zum Tode, Endlichkeit; Latin: vanitas, memento mori; Hebrew: hevel [vapour, futility]; Pali: anicca; Chinese: wuchang [impermanence]; Japanese: mujō.
Phrases: memento mori [Lat.]; vanitas vanitatum, omnia vanitas [Lat.] [Bible]; golden lads and girls all must, as chimney-sweepers, come to dust [Cymbeline]; all that lives must die, passing through nature to eternity [Hamlet]; et in Arcadia ego [Lat.].

Head: The Immediacy of Finitude
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › b. Finitude › iii. Finitude as Such › 1. The Immediacy of Finitude
Gloss: The limited thing as simply given: something whose very being is to perish.
Nouns: immediacy of finitude; the merely finite, sheer finitude, bare mortality; fixed finitude, hardened finitude, the finite as absolute; despair of the finite, melancholy, sadness, mourning; perishing as essence; fatalism, resignation, acceptance of mortality; nothingness of the finite, nullity, vanity &c H0019. immediate finitude, the perishable, perishing, the hour of birth as the hour of death, the given finite.
Verbs: be merely finite, be nothing but mortal; perish, waste away; insist on finitude, hold fast to the finite, cling to the finite. pass away, cease.
Adjective: merely finite, purely mortal, irredeemably finite; ephemeral, fleeting; melancholy, mournful, elegiac, resigned, fatalistic. transient, transitory, passing. perishable, immediate.
Adverbs: merely, only, no more than; in the end; irrevocably, without remedy. transiently, perishably.
Phrases: all is vanity and vexation of spirit [Bible]; out, out, brief candle [Macbeth]; sunt lacrimae rerum et mentem mortalia tangunt [Lat.] [Virgil].

Head: Limitation and the Ought
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › b. Finitude › iii. Finitude as Such › 2. Limitation and the Ought
Gloss: The limit felt as a barrier to be overcome, and the demand to overcome it. What a thing ought to be stands against what it is.
Nouns: limitation, barrier, bar, obstacle, check, hindrance, impediment, constraint, restraint, restriction, confinement, fetter, shackle, trammel; ceiling, glass ceiling, cap; the ought, ought, oughtness, obligation, demand, requirement, imperative, exigency, norm, standard, ideal &c H0756; aspiration, striving, yearning, longing; the gap between is and ought, is-ought gap; vocation, task, mission, calling; deontology, deontic. let, knot, knag†, hitch, contretemps, screw loose, grit in the oil. prevention, preclusion, obstruction, stricture, restraint &c H0645. bond. coercion &c H0645, cohibition†, repression, suppression, discipline, control. deterrent, hamper, roadblock, blockage.
Verbs: limit, restrict, confine, bar, check, hinder, constrain, restrain, hem in, cramp, curb, fetter, trammel; strive, aspire, yearn, long, reach for, reach beyond; ought, should, must, be obliged, be bound, be called upon; transgress, overstep, exceed, surpass, push the envelope. retard, preclude, inhibit &c H0701, shackle &c H0645. hold back, hold in check, keep within bounds. impede, obstruct.
Adjective: limited, restricted, confined, hemmed in, cramped, constrained; obligatory, binding, incumbent, mandatory, imperative, normative, deontic, prescriptive; aspiring, striving, yearning, unfulfilled, unrealized, ideal. incumbent on, under obligation, bound by.
Adverbs: as it ought to be, as it should be, by rights, in principle, ideally. within limits, as it ought.
Foreign: German: das Sollen, Streben, Sehnsucht, Schranke; Latin: nisus, de jure; Sanskrit: dharma [duty]; Chinese: dao [the way one ought to go].
Phrases: du kannst, denn du sollst [Ger.] [Schiller, on Kant]; a man's reach should exceed his grasp, or what's a heaven for? [Browning]; ad astra per aspera [Lat.]; ultra posse nemo obligatur [Lat.].

Head: Transition of the Finite into the Infinite
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › b. Finitude › iii. Finitude as Such › 3. Transition of the Finite into the Infinite
Gloss: The way a limited thing, by pushing against its limit, goes beyond itself and points toward what has no limit.
Nouns: transition of the finite into the infinite; self-transcendence, self-overcoming, self-surpassing; transgression, overstepping, overstepping of bounds, going beyond, exceeding, excess; elevation, ascent, ascension, uplift, exaltation, sublimation, rise; transcendence, transcendency, surpassing; apotheosis, deification; liberation; breakthrough, breakout, crossing, passage. the passage of the finite into the infinite, going beyond the limit, the self-sublation of the finite. jailbreak.
Verbs: transcend, surpass, exceed, overstep, overpass, outrun, outgrow, go beyond, get beyond, rise above, rise beyond, break through, break out, cross over; self-transcend, overcome oneself; elevate, exalt, sublimate; point beyond. overreach, overleap. transgress. transcend itself, pass over.
Adjective: self-transcending, self-surpassing, transcendent, transcending, liminal, transitional, transgressive; aspiring, upward, ascending, anagogic, anagogical. passing.
Adverbs: beyond, over and above, past; upward, onward, higher. beyond itself, into the infinite.
Foreign: German: Selbstüberwindung; Latin: excelsior; Greek: anabasis, epektasis [stretching forward], theōsis; Arabic: fanāʾ; Sanskrit: mokṣa [release], nirvāṇa.
Phrases: excelsior [Lat.]; man is something that shall be overcome [Nietzsche]; per aspera ad astra [Lat.]; plus ultra [Lat.].

Head: Infinity
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › c. Infinity
Gloss: That which is not limited by anything outside it; boundlessness.
Nouns: infinity, infinitude, the infinite; boundlessness, limitlessness, endlessness, illimitability, immeasurability, immensity, vastness, unboundedness, eternity &c; the unbounded, the unlimited, the endless; absolute, perfection, plenitude. infiniteness, perpetuity &c H0222. infinity &c H0053. unlimitedness.
Verbs: be infinite, have no limit, know no bounds, be without end, stretch to infinity, extend indefinitely. know no limits, have no limits, have no bounds, go on for ever. transcend, exceed all bounds.
Adjective: infinite, boundless, limitless, endless, unbounded, unlimited, illimitable, immeasurable, measureless, incalculable, innumerable, numberless, countless, inexhaustible, interminable, unending, never-ending, everlasting, eternal, perpetual; vast, immense, unfathomable, fathomless, bottomless; absolute, unconditioned. uncircumscribed, boundless &c H0053. inconceivable.
Adverbs: infinitely, endlessly &c adj.; world without end, without limit, without end. boundlessly.

Head: The Infinite in General
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › c. Infinity › i. The Infinite in General
Gloss: The unlimited in its first, simple sense: what the limited passes into when it goes beyond itself; the negation of the finite, taken as what truly is.
Nouns: the infinite in general; the beyond, beyondness, transcendence, the transcendent, the other world, otherworldliness, the hereafter, yonder, the great beyond; the unconditioned, the absolute other, the wholly other; the not-finite, the nonfinite, negation of the finite; empyrean, heaven, the heavens; ideal, the ideal; true being. the infinite as such, the unlimited, the non-finite.
Verbs: lie beyond, transcend, surpass, be other than, stand beyond, tower above. exceed, overpass. negate the finite.
Adjective: infinite, transcendent, transcendental, otherworldly, supramundane, supernal, celestial, ultramundane, beyond; unconditioned, absolute, ultimate; negative, apophatic. distant, remote, ulterior. unearthly. unlimited.
Adverbs: beyond, in the beyond, yonder, over yonder, hereafter, in the hereafter; out of this world. far off, afar. without limit.
Foreign: German: das Jenseits, das ganz Andere, das Unendliche überhaupt; Arabic: al-ghayb [the unseen]; Sanskrit: paramārtha [ultimate].
Phrases: beyond the beyond; my kingdom is not of this world [Bible]; the undiscovered country from whose bourn no traveller returns [Hamlet].

Head: Alternating Determination of the Finite and the Infinite
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › c. Infinity › ii. Alternating Determination of the Finite and the Infinite
Gloss: The unlimited held apart from the limited, which makes it limited in turn; an endless alternation between the two, like a series that never arrives. Also called the bad or spurious infinite.
Nouns: alternating determination of the finite and the infinite; bad infinity, spurious infinity; endless progression, infinite progress, infinite regress, regress, endless regress; perpetual ought, endless striving; vicious circle, merry-go-round, treadmill, rat race, squirrel cage, Sisyphean labour; Sisyphus, the stone of Sisyphus, Tantalus, the Danaids' sieve; tedium, monotony, repetition, iteration, sameness, ad nauseam; asymptote, horizon, mirage, receding goal, will-o'-the-wisp; turtles all the way down. recurrence, succession. the bad infinite, the spurious infinite, the endless progress, the alternation, the ought.
Verbs: alternate, oscillate, seesaw, shuttle, ping-pong, go back and forth, swing to and fro, see-saw; regress, recede; repeat, reiterate, iterate; go on forever, go round in circles, chase one's tail, run in place, tread water; never arrive. fluctuate, waver, vacillate, turn and turn about. go on endlessly.
Adjective: endless, unending, interminable, never-ending, perpetual, ceaseless, incessant, sempiternal; repetitive, iterative, monotonous, tedious, Sisyphean, Tantalean; asymptotic, receding; alternating, oscillating, oscillatory, reciprocating; spurious, false, bad, vicious. recursive [Comp.]. tiresome, insistent.
Adverbs: without end, on and on, again and again, over and over, round and round, back and forth, to and fro, hither and thither; et cetera, and so on, and so forth, and so on and so forth. backwards and forwards. alternately. repeatedly.
Foreign: German: schlechte Unendlichkeit, die schlechte Unendlichkeit, Wechselbestimmung; Latin: progressus in infinitum, regressus in infinitum, circulus vitiosus, ignis fatuus, ad infinitum, ad nauseam; Arabic: tasalsul [infinite chain]; Sanskrit: saṃsāra [cycle of rebirth], anavasthā [infinite regress].
Phrases: turtles all the way down; great fleas have little fleas upon their backs to bite 'em [Augustus De Morgan]; who will guard the guards themselves? quis custodiet ipsos custodes? [Lat.] [Juvenal]; the more things change, the more they stay the same.

Head: Affirmative Infinity
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › c. Infinity › iii. Affirmative Infinity
Gloss: The unlimited understood as including the limited rather than lying beyond it; completeness rather than endlessness. Pictured as a circle, as against an endless line.
Nouns: affirmative infinity, true infinity, genuine infinite; actual infinite, completed infinite; circle, cycle, ring, orb, sphere, round, closed curve, serpent swallowing its tail; return, homecoming, self-return; wholeness, totality, completeness, entirety, fullness, plenitude, perfection, consummation; self-containment, self-sufficiency, autarky; the whole; mandala; eternity, eternal now. integrity, unity &c H0031, completeness &c H0120, integration. hoop, annulus, loop, wheel, orbit. circuit. fullness &c H0120. the true infinite, the affirmative infinite.
Verbs: return, come round, come full circle, close the circle, round off, complete, consummate, perfect; include, embrace, encompass, comprehend, contain. comprise. include &c H0144. enclose, encircle. return into itself.
Adjective: infinite, true, genuine, actual; circular, cyclic, cyclical, orbicular, spherical, rounded, self-returning, self-enclosed, self-contained, self-sufficient; whole, entire, complete, total, integral, perfect, consummate; all-embracing, all-encompassing, comprehensive. annular. complete &c H0120. whole &c H0120, perfect &c H0197, absolute, plenary. truly infinite.

Phrases: in my end is my beginning [T. S. Eliot]; das Wahre ist das Ganze [Ger.] [Hegel]; God is an infinite sphere whose centre is everywhere and circumference nowhere [Liber XXIV philosophorum].

Head: Being-for-Self
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › γ. Being-for-Self
Gloss: Self-containedness; the condition of a thing that relates only to itself, holding whatever is other within itself as an aspect of its own; independence.
Nouns: being-for-self, being for itself; self-relation, self-reference, self-relatedness, reflexivity; independence, self-sufficiency, self-subsistence, self-containment, autonomy, autarky, aseity; individuality, selfhood, ipseity; completeness, wholeness, integrity, closure; ideality; being-in-and-for-itself. totality, entirety, unity &c H0031. self-containedness, being-for-itself, the for-itself.
Verbs: be for oneself, be by oneself, stand alone, stand on one's own feet, be self-sufficient, be one's own master; relate to oneself, refer to oneself; return into oneself, withdraw into oneself. be for itself, relate to itself.
Adjective: self-relating, self-referential, reflexive, self-contained, self-sufficient, self-subsistent, self-standing, self-reliant, independent, autonomous, autarkic, autarkical, sovereign; individual, singular; complete, whole, closed, rounded; ideal. integral. entire, undivided. for-itself.

Head: Being-for-Self as Such
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › γ. Being-for-Self › a. Being-for-Self as Such

Nouns: being-for-self as such; pure self-relation, simple self-reference; returned-into-self, closure, self-enclosure, insularity; ideality of the finite; independence &c H0027; infinite self-relation; sufficiency, completeness. being-for-self in general, self-relation, the infinite return into self, the for-itself.
Verbs: return into oneself, close upon oneself, be complete in oneself, need nothing else. relate to itself, be for itself, return into itself.
Adjective: self-enclosed, self-sufficient, self-complete, complete in itself, needing nothing, insular, closed, sealed, hermetic. self-related, self-contained, complete.

Head: Determinate Being and Being-for-Self
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › γ. Being-for-Self › a. Being-for-Self as Such › i. Determinate Being and Being-for-Self

Head: Being-for-One
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › γ. Being-for-Self › a. Being-for-Self as Such › ii. Being-for-One

Hegel definition: The laughable is any contrast between the substantial and its appearance, between an end and its means, in which the appearance cancels itself, so that realizing the end is the end's own undoing. Comedy makes this its principle. It makes the subject master of everything that counts as essential in what it wills, and lets its aims, being without substance, perish through its own willing and through outward chance alike. The subject does not perish with them: in their dissolution it enjoys itself, untroubled, as the infinite power over every finite content. In tragedy substantial ends destroy one another; in comedy what is null destroys itself, and the self survives it, cheerful, as the absolute. With this, art dissolves itself.
Hegel quotes:
Every contrast between something substantive and its appearance, between an end and the means, may be laughable; this is a contradiction in which the appearance cancels itself and the realization of an end is at the same time the end’s own destruction.
— Aesthetics, Dramatic Poetry: the principle of comedy (tr. Knox)
A world in which man as subject or person has made himself completely master of everything that counts to him otherwise as the essence of what he wills and accomplishes, a world whose aims are therefore self-destructive because they are unsubstantial.
— Aesthetics, Dramatic Poetry: the principle of comedy (tr. Knox)
[The principle for comedy is when] the mastery of all relations and ends is given as much to the individual in his willing and action, as to external contingency.
— Aesthetics, Dramatic Poetry (tr. Knox)
As regards the mental side of these phenomena, we know with regard to laughter that it is generated by an immediately obvious contradiction, by something turning at once into its opposite, hence by something immediately self-annihilating, -assuming that we are not involved in this null content, do not regard it as our own; for if we felt ourselves injured by the destruction of this content, then we should weep. If, for example, someone proudly striding along falls over, this can give rise to laughter over it, because he experiences in his person the simple dialectic that what happens to him is the opposite of what he intended. Hence what provokes laughter in genuine comedies also essentially lies in the immediate veering round of a purpose in itself null into its opposite; whereas in tragedy it is substantial purposes which destroy themselves in their mutual opposition. With the dialectic befalling the object of comedy, the subjectivity of the spectator or listener attains to a serene and untroubled enjoyment of itself, since it is the absolute ideality, the infinite power over every limited content, consequently the pure dialectic by which, in fact, the comic object is annihilated. Herein lies the ground of the gaiety into which we are transported by the comic. But the physiological appearance of this gaiety, which particularly interests us here, is in harmony with this ground. For in laughter, the subjectivity attaining to untroubled enjoyment of itself, this pure self, this spiritual light, embodies itself as a glow spreading over the countenance, and at the same time the spiritual act by which the soul repels the ridiculous from itself finds a bodily expression in the forcibly interrupted expulsion of the breath.
— Encyclopedia, Philosophy of Spirit §401, Addition (tr. Wallace and Miller)

Gloss: The thinker who turned philosophy into a critique of reason, showing that the mind supplies the forms and categories of experience, so that we know things only as they appear, never as they are in themselves.
Nouns: Kant; the critical turn that asks how knowledge is possible, the critique of pure reason, transcendental idealism, the thing in itself, phenomena and noumena, the categories, the synthetic a priori, the categorical imperative, autonomy, the sublime, transcendental aesthetic, transcendental analytic, Determining judgment, Reflective judgment, faculties, sensibility.
Verbs: critique, limit, legislate, deduce.
Adjective: Kantian, critical, transcendental, deontological.
Adverbs: transcendentally, critically.
Foreign: German: Ding an sich [thing-in-itself], Anschauung [Intuition].
Phrases: thoughts without content are empty, intuitions without concepts are blind [Kant]; sapere aude [Lat.].

Head: Fichte
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › iii. Philosophy › β. History of Philosophy [Tetrad] › d. Modern Philosophy › iii. Critical Philosophy (German Idealism) › 2. Fichte
Gloss: The thinker who removed the unknowable thing-in-itself and derived the whole world of experience from the activity of the self, which sets itself up and marks out its own limits.
Nouns: Fichte; the self-positing I, the I and the not-I, subjective idealism, striving, the vocation of man, intellectual intuition, productive imagination.
Verbs: posit, strive, act.
Adjective: Fichtean, subjective, activist.
Adverbs: by self-positing.
Foreign: German: das Ich, Wissenschaftslehre [science of knowledge], Tathandlung [deed-act], Anstoß [check], intellektuelle Anschauung [intellectual intuition], Produktive Einbildungskraft [productive imagination].
Phrases: the I posits itself [Fichte]; what sort of philosophy one chooses depends on what sort of person one is [Fichte].

Head: Schelling
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › iii. Philosophy › β. History of Philosophy [Tetrad] › d. Modern Philosophy › iii. Critical Philosophy (German Idealism) › 3. Schelling
Gloss: The thinker who treated nature and mind as two expressions of a single underlying identity, so that nature is visible mind and mind is invisible nature.
Nouns: Schelling; philosophy of nature, the absolute as indifference of subject and object, identity philosophy, intellectual intuition, art as organ of philosophy, the late philosophy of revelation, potencies, powers.
Verbs: intuit, identify, unite.
Adjective: Schellingian, romantic, organic, intuitive.
Adverbs: intuitively.
Foreign: German: Naturphilosophie, Identitätsphilosophie, Indifferenz [nondifference], Potenzen [potencies].
Phrases: nature is visible spirit, spirit invisible nature [Schelling]; the night in which all cows are black [Hegel].
